title: Listening for what is not said
description: Sometimes the most important part of a conversation is the topic that keeps quietly changing.

body.heading: Notice the swerve
paragraphs: If every mention of a job, a person, or a plan gets quickly steered away from, the steering itself is information. You do not need to name it like a detective. Just notice, and soften.
People swerve for many reasons: it hurts, it is private, or they have not found words yet. All three deserve gentleness rather than pursuit.

body.heading: Offer, never corner
paragraphs: If you sense something unsaid, make one light offer: “If you ever want to talk about the new job, I’m around.” Then let it drop. An offer can be accepted weeks later; a cornering is remembered immediately.
Curiosity is a gift when it is invited and a burden when it is not. The same question can be either, depending on whether the person can decline it for free.

body.heading: Respect the closed door
paragraphs: Some things are not said because they are not yours to hear, and that is not a rejection of you. Privacy is not distance; it is part of how trust is built.
The friend who does not pry becomes the friend who is eventually told. Patience is the price of being trusted with the real story.

takeaway: Notice the swerves, make one light offer, and let closed doors stay closed until they open on their own.
